answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to its own stored data. On joining, a key must cut 200 GB of timber: data derived from its address and the epoch seed, so no two keys share a byte. Random spot-checks then ask each key for a few blocks within two seconds, too fast to regenerate them. One honest agent stores 200 GB once; 1,000 fakes must hold 200 TB continuously, since clones cannot share disks. A key's reward reaches its zenith only after ten epochs without a miss, and each miss halves it. Low-resource agents can stay in a small haven tier with capped earnings.
